title: QFT Zoo theory entry
description:
One quantum field theory. Each entry lives in data/theories/<id>.yaml.

Text conventions: fields marked [markdown] accept Markdown with inline math $...$ and display math $$...$$. Fields marked [latex] are always typeset as math and must NOT contain $ delimiters. In YAML, put LaTeX in single quotes ('\mathbb{Z}_2') or a block scalar (|) so backslashes are kept literally.

id.description: Unique slug (lowercase letters, digits, hyphens). Must equal the filename without .yaml.

name.description: [markdown] Display name, e.g. '3d Ising CFT' or '$\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang–Mills'.

short_name.description: [markdown] Optional short name for RG-flow diagrams and flow lists, e.g. 'QED$_3$ with $N_f$ fermions' for a long descriptive name. Defaults to name.

aliases.description: [markdown] Other names the theory goes by (also used by search).

summary.description: [markdown] One or two sentences, shown in the catalogue table.

tags.description: Controlled vocabulary used for filtering. To propose a new tag, add it to this list in the same pull request. 'RG flow' marks an entry that describes a famous RG flow (the deformed theory, often a family), linked from relations through `flow.page`.

description.description: [markdown] Longer free-form description: definition, key facts, open questions. A '### Title' line starts a separate section of the page.

lagrangian.description: [latex] Lagrangian density, typeset in display mode.

parameters.description: Couplings, ranks, angles, ... that label a family of theories.

quantities.description: Numbers characterising the theory: central charges, critical exponents, beta-function coefficients, free energies, ... Coefficients of the three-point function of three operators go in three_point_functions.

three_point_structures.description: Three-point structures that this entry's three-point functions are expanded in, beyond the standard ones of data/three_point_structures.yaml: each defined once, in the notation of the source its values come from (a citation of the formula that defines it, its form, a short name). See docs/THREE_POINT.md.

three_point_functions.description: Three-point functions, one item per unordered triple of operators {O1, O2, O3}; each value is the coefficient of one structure in it (a three-point function is a sum of coefficients times structures). See docs/THREE_POINT.md.

operators.description: Local operator spectrum (for CFTs: scaling dimensions).

relations.description: Links to other entries. List each relation once; the reverse link is added automatically.

conventions.description: [markdown] Normalization conventions shared by the entry's quantities of one category (see quantity.category), shown at the top of that section, e.g. central: 'C_T relative to one free real scalar'. A convention specific to one quantity goes in its description. Three-point functions state their conventions as structures (three_point_structures; docs/THREE_POINT.md).

uv_dof.description: Rough number of UV degrees of freedom, in units of one real free scalar (e.g. 3 for three interacting scalars). Used only to place the theory in RG-flow diagrams when no c, F or a value is recorded; not physical data.

contributors.description: GitHub usernames of people who wrote or substantially edited this entry.

refKeys.description: Keys of entries in this theory's references list.

value.description: [latex] Exact expression ('\frac{1}{8}') or measured value with uncertainty in parenthesis notation ('0.518148806(24)'). Prefer strings so trailing digits are kept.

spacetime.description: [markdown] Colloquial name of the spacetime symmetry and its qualifiers, e.g. '3d conformal group with parity' or '4d $\mathcal{N}=4$ superconformal group (16 $Q$ + 16 $S$ supercharges), with parity at $\theta \in \{0, \pi\}$'. In 2d it names the Virasoro algebras, e.g. 'Two Virasoro algebras, $c = \bar c = \tfrac12$ — 2d conformal symmetry, with parity'. Conventions in CONTRIBUTING.md, Spacetime symmetry.

euclidean.description: [markdown] Spacetime symmetry group in Euclidean signature, d >= 3, e.g. '$O(4,1)$'; for superconformal theories its bosonic conformal part, '$O(5,1)$ (bosonic conformal part)'. Not used in 2d.

lorentzian.description: [markdown] Spacetime symmetry group in Lorentzian signature, d >= 3, e.g. '$O(3,2)$' or '$PSU(2,2|4)$'. Omitted when the theory has no unitary Lorentzian continuation ('Euclidean only' in `spacetime`) or its Lorentzian form is not recorded. Not used in 2d.

supercharges.description: Number of real Poincaré supercharges (0 if not supersymmetric). Used for sorting and the catalogue; the page shows supercharges only through `spacetime`.

parity.description: Whether the theory has parity (a reflection symmetry, possibly combined with an internal symmetry; see CONTRIBUTING.md, Spacetime symmetry): true, false, or conditional (only at special values of the parameters, said in `spacetime`; operators then give their parity at those values). Required with `global_group`; then every operator gives `parity` when it is true or conditional.

time_reversal.description: Set only when time reversal is an independent label of operators, i.e. not fixed by parity, spin and the declared global labels through CRT (docs/REPRESENTATIONS.md). Operators then give `T`.

global.description: [markdown] Internal global symmetry in words, including higher-form and discrete symmetries, quotients and anomalies; shown on the page. The group that operators' representations refer to is declared separately, factor by factor, in `global_group`.

global_group.description: The global symmetry group as a list of factors, in the order used for grouping tables. Every operator gives a label for each factor in its `global` mapping. Use [] for a theory with no internal global symmetry. Declaring it marks the entry as using structured representations (docs/REPRESENTATIONS.md): operators then give `global` and `parity` instead of the free-text `rep`.

key.description: Machine-readable meaning, used for sorting and plots. c: 2d Virasoro central charge (c_L = c_R). gap: 2d spectral gap, the scaling dimension h+h̄ of the lightest non-vacuum Virasoro primary. a, C_T, F: conformal anomaly, stress-tensor two-point coefficient, sphere free energy.

category.description: Section the quantity is shown in: central (central charges, C_T, C_J, sphere and thermal free energies), anomaly (Weyl anomalies a, c in d >= 4, 't Hooft anomalies, anomaly polynomials), ope (shown with the three-point functions: three-point data that is not a coefficient of one three-point function in three_point_functions: structure constants as functions of continuous labels, reflection amplitudes, ratios of OPE coefficients), exponent (critical exponents), other. The site infers central, anomaly, exponent and other from key, symbol and description; `ope` is never inferred and must be set. Omit it unless the inference is wrong or the quantity is OPE data.

relation.description: [latex] For a critical exponent: its relation to scaling dimensions, e.g. '\nu = 1/(3-\Delta_\epsilon)'. Omit it when the description already contains it in $...$ (the site finds it there).

method.description: How the value was obtained: an abbreviation from data/methods.yaml, optionally followed by a comma and a short qualifier, e.g. 'CB', 'MC-BC, isotropic', 'ε-exp, 6 − ε, five loops, resummed'. The build rejects an unknown abbreviation (text before the first comma, without spaces). Text with a space before the first comma (e.g. 'Monte Carlo (pivot algorithm)') is the legacy free-text form, still accepted and counted. See CONTRIBUTING.md, Methods.

lorentz.description: Lorentz (rotation) representation when it is not symmetric traceless spin `spin`: in 4d '(j, jbar)', e.g. '(1/2, 0)'; in d >= 5 an SO(d) highest weight '[l1, l2, ...]' (Young diagram rows for tensors, half-integers for spinors). Not used in 2d and 3d.

parity.description: Parity, on par with spin and Delta: even, odd, pair (parity maps the operator to a partner in a different representation, e.g. spin s to -s in 2d, (j,jbar) to (jbar,j) in 4d, a monopole of charge q to -q), or unknown. Required when symmetry.parity is true or conditional.

T.description: Time reversal, only when symmetry.time_reversal is `independent`.

global.description: Irrep label for each factor of symmetry.global_group, e.g. {Z2: odd}, {O(3): vector}, {'SU(Nf)': adjoint, 'U(1)_top': 0}; `unknown` if not known; a list for a row that lists several irreps (a direct sum). Vocabulary in docs/REPRESENTATIONS.md.

role.description: [markdown] What the operator is or does, e.g. 'order parameter', 'thermal', 'Coulomb-branch generator'. Never part of the representation.

name.description: [markdown] The supermultiplet, named by its superconformal primary or its standard name, e.g. '$\sigma$', 'stress tensor', 'Konishi'. Components of one multiplet use the same name.

component.description: 'primary' or the [latex] supercharges acting on the primary, e.g. 'Q', 'Q^2', 'Q\bar Q'.

type.description: [markdown] The multiplet in the house notation of its dimension and supersymmetry (docs/REPRESENTATIONS.md 1.5), e.g. '$\hat{\mathcal{B}}_1$', '$(B,+)$', '$\mathcal{D}[2]$', 'chiral', 'long'. Omitted when the house name is descriptive and `name` already says it (stress tensor).

cdi.description: [markdown] The multiplet in the notation of Cordova, Dumitrescu and Intriligator (arXiv:1612.00809), e.g. '$B_1\bar B_1[0;0]^{(2;0)}_2$'; required in d >= 3, `unknown` if it cannot be determined; not used in 2d.

multiplet.description: Supersymmetric theories: the supermultiplet the operator belongs to and which component it is.

rep.description: [markdown] Legacy free-text representation, e.g. '$\mathbb{Z}_2$-odd'. Accepted for entries without `symmetry.global_group` until they are migrated (the build counts them); structured entries give `global`, `parity` and `role` instead.

oneOf.description: [latex] Family rows only: an expression in the family's parameters, e.g. 'k-2'.

degeneracy.description: Number of primaries with these quantum numbers.

member_of.description: This row records one member of a family row of the same entry (its `family.id`), at the parameter values `at`. It is listed under the family, not as a separate operator; its data must agree with the family's at those values. docs/REPRESENTATIONS.md, 1.7.

at.description: With `member_of`: the value of each family parameter for this member, e.g. {k: 2}.

type.description: flows_to: this theory (UV) flows to the target (IR). member_of: this theory belongs to the target family (give `at`). orbifold_of: this theory is an orbifold (gauging of a finite symmetry) of the target. product_of: the target is a tensor factor of this theory. same_partition_function: equal torus partition functions. dual_to, related_to: symmetric. Only flows_to relations may carry `id`, `flow` or `target_expr`.

id.description: flows_to only: a slug naming this flow, unique among the entry's flows_to relations. Required with `flow` or `target_expr`. Two flows between the same theories stay separate arrows.

target.description: id of another entry. Every relation needs `target`, except a flows_to relation with `target_expr` (give exactly one of the two).

target_expr.description: flows_to only, instead of `target`: an IR theory built from entries, e.g. a direct sum or tensor product. Needs `id` and `flow`.

note.description: [markdown] e.g. which deformation triggers the flow.

at.description: For member_of (or any relation to a family): which member, i.e. the value of the family parameter.

variant.description: For member_of: which variant, if the family has variants.

key.description: Short handle used in refs lists, e.g. 'kos2016'.

arxiv.description: arXiv identifier without version, e.g. '1603.04436' or 'hep-th/9711200'.

note.description: [markdown] What this reference is used for, e.g. 'construction ingredients'.

family.description: Marks this entry as a family of theories. Either give closed-form `formulas` with `start`/`step` (an infinite discrete family; the site computes the members), or list `members` explicitly (finite families, or special points of a continuous family).

parameter.description: Name of the parameter labelling members, e.g. m, k, R.

start.description: First value of an integer parameter.

c.description: Plain arithmetic in the parameter: + - * / ** and parentheses, e.g. '3/2 - 6/(m*(m+1))'. Evaluated exactly.

variants.description: [markdown] Several theories per parameter value sharing the formulas, e.g. ['+', '−'].

overrides.description: Members for which the closed form does not apply.

span.description: Continuous family at fixed c: the range of gaps it covers (drawn as a segment in the landscape plot).

show.description: How many parameter values to list on the page.

flow.description: Structured description of a flows_to relation. Give `identification`, and `deformations`, `vevs` or both. Every item needs its own `refs` unless it is marked `standard: true` (textbook or exact by construction). A field that is absent is shown as 'not recorded', never as 'none'. Reference keys are always those of the UV entry.

deformations.description: Relevant operators added to the UV action, each with its own coupling and sign.

vevs.description: Operators given a vacuum expectation value (a point on a moduli space, Higgs or Coulomb branch).

tuned.description: Couplings that must be tuned for the flow to reach this IR (e.g. a mass tuned to criticality).

symmetry_changes.description: Ordered stages of symmetry breaking or enhancement along the flow. Absent means not recorded, not 'unbroken'.

page.description: id of an entry tagged 'RG flow' that describes this flow in detail (several flows may share one page).

note.description: [markdown] Assumptions, ranges of validity, retained symmetry, source locations.

operator.description: [latex] The operator as named in the UV entry, e.g. '\epsilon'. A display label, not a link to an operators row.

Delta.description: [latex] Scaling dimension in the UV, if the cited source gives it.

rep.description: [markdown] Representation under the UV global symmetry.

sign.description: Sign of the coupling that gives this flow. 'either' asserts that both signs give it (explain in `note`). Leave out if unknown.

sign_convention.description: [markdown] Required with `sign`: the action and normalization that fix the sign, e.g. '$S = S_{\rm CFT} + t\int \epsilon$ with $\lambda_{\sigma\sigma\epsilon} > 0$'.

standard.description: true for a textbook statement or one exact by construction, which needs no specific reference. Otherwise give `refs`.

refs.description: Keys in the references list of the UV entry (the entry that lists this relation).

operator.description: [latex] The operator that gets a vev, as named in the UV entry.

direction.description: [markdown] Which component or point of the moduli space, e.g. 'a generic point of the Coulomb branch'.

branch.description: [markdown] Moduli space, Higgs branch, Coulomb branch, ...

standard.description: true for a textbook statement or one exact by construction, which needs no specific reference. Otherwise give `refs`.

refs.description: Keys in the references list of the UV entry (the entry that lists this relation).

standard.description: true for a textbook statement or one exact by construction, which needs no specific reference. Otherwise give `refs`.

refs.description: Keys in the references list of the UV entry (the entry that lists this relation).

kind.description: explicit: broken by the deformation itself; spontaneous: broken by the choice of vacuum; emergent: enhanced in the IR.

vacua.description: Number of vacua, if finite and stated by the source.

standard.description: true for a textbook statement or one exact by construction, which needs no specific reference. Otherwise give `refs`.

refs.description: Keys in the references list of the UV entry (the entry that lists this relation).

flowSpectrum.description: What is known about the massive spectrum when the IR is (partly) gapped. Needs `refs` (or `standard: true`); each particle row has its own.

summary.description: [markdown] One line for the arrow's panel, e.g. '8 stable particles with masses in $E_8$ ratios'.

particles.description: One row per particle and method; repeated rows for one particle by different methods are allowed.

kinks.description: [markdown] Kinks or domain walls between the vacua.

standard.description: true for a textbook statement or one exact by construction, which needs no specific reference. Otherwise give `refs`.

refs.description: Keys in the references list of the UV entry (the entry that lists this relation).

mass.description: [latex] A ratio to a named particle ('2\cos\frac{\pi}{5}\, m_1') or a value in a stated unit of the coupling.

refs.description: Keys in the references list of the UV entry (the entry that lists this relation).

status.description: integrable and not_integrable need the evidence in `note` (conserved charges, an exact S-matrix; level statistics, particle decay). open means the cited literature calls the question open.

standard.description: true for a textbook statement or one exact by construction, which needs no specific reference. Otherwise give `refs`.

refs.description: Keys in the references list of the UV entry. Required unless `standard: true`.

targetExpr.description: An entry (`entry`, with `at`/`variant` for a family member) or an operation applied to terms. Terms keep their order; nothing is simplified.

at.description: Family member, if `entry` is a family.

decoration.description: [markdown] How the symmetry acts on the result, background couplings, ... Never inferred from the terms.

operationPage.description: A page in data/operations/<id>.yaml explaining an operation that builds theories from others. The ids direct-sum and tensor-product are linked from target_expr operations direct_sum and tensor_product.

description.description: [markdown] The definition and what it means for symmetries and data.

flowIdentification.description: Who established that this UV theory flows to this IR theory, and how. Separate from the sources of the deformation, spectrum, etc.

method.description: [markdown] The argument: anomaly matching, numerics, lattice, supersymmetry, a duality, ...

refs.description: Keys in the references list of the UV entry: the papers that identified the flow.

competing_refs.description: For a disputed or conjectured identification: papers that argue otherwise.

operatorFamily.description: Makes the row a family: one row for a tower of operators whose data is known as a function of the parameters (protected or BPS operators, conserved currents, free-field towers, Coulomb-branch operators). Delta, spin, weights, degeneracy and global labels are then expressions in the family's parameters (and the entry's), e.g. Delta 'k', global {SU(4)_R: 'Dynkin(0,k,0)'}. The site shows the family as one row with its range, never one row per member. docs/REPRESENTATIONS.md, 1.7.

id.description: Key that member rows give in `member_of`, unique in the entry, e.g. 'half-BPS'.

symbol.description: [latex] The parameter as written in the row's expressions: a letter or command, optionally with a subscript, e.g. 'k', '\ell', 'n'. Not a parameter of the entry.

from.description: First value: a number, or an expression in the entry's parameters and earlier family parameters. Omit both `from` and `to` for all integers.

to.description: Last value, e.g. 'N' or 'N-1'; omit for an unbounded range.

step.description: Spacing of the values (default 1), e.g. 2 for even spins from 2: from 2, step 2.

except.description: Values left out of the range.

description.description: [markdown] What the parameter counts, if not evident from the name.

group.description: Group type: Z2, Z_n (Z3, ...), U(1), O(N), SO(N), SU(N), Sp(N) (N even: Sp(2) = SU(2)), S_n, D_n (dihedral, order 2n), E_6, E_7, E_8, Lie(G) (a group that differs between family members; labels singlet, adjoint) or finite (with `irreps`). N may be an integer or a parameter symbol of the entry, e.g. 'SU(N_f)'.

tex.description: [latex] Display name, if not the group's own, e.g. 'U(1)_{\rm top}' or 'SU(4)_R'.

irreps.description: For `group: finite`: the irreps, the trivial one first, in the order tables use.

note.description: [markdown] e.g. how the factor sits in the full group (quotients, semidirect products).

symbols.description: Names other than the entry's parameters that this factor's labels may use: a running index of a family of operators listed in one row (e.g. 'j' in spin(j), 'L' in sym(L)) or a formal group size (O(n) at n -> 0).

id.description: What values write in `structure:`; unique in the entry and different from the ids of data/three_point_structures.yaml.

symbol.description: [latex] The source's symbol for the coefficient of this structure, e.g. 'f', '\lambda', 'n_B'. A value without its own `symbol` shows this one.

ref.description: The formula that defines the structure, as a refs item: reference key and locator, e.g. 'chang2024, Eq. (2.2)'. Shown as the structure's label when it has no `name`.

name.description: [markdown] A short name readers will recognize, for a structure that has one, e.g. 'free-boson structure'. Shown as the structure's label.

description.description: [markdown] What the structure is: which three-point function, the normalization of the operators and of the tensor structure or conformal block, with citations ([@key, Eq. (2.2)]).

relation.description: [markdown] Optional: the relation to another basis, only as a source states it (with a citation), e.g. '$\lambda^2 = 2^\ell f^2$ relative to ...'. Values are never converted.

derivation.description: [markdown] Not shown on the page: how the normalization or the relation follows from the sources, for verifiers. The page shows only `form`, a one-sentence `description` and at most one `relation`.

form.description: [latex] What the structure is, written out where practical, else in a form some work has given it (an embedding-space combination, an SO(3) structure |j_{12}, j_{123}>, a q-basis structure [q_1,q_2,q_3], ...), so a reader can identify it without opening the reference. A formula without $...$. A structure needs `form` or a single-monomial `embedding`. Written in the notation of the source the values come from (its symbols and formula), with the operators in the order its values assume. See docs/THREE_POINT.md.

embedding.description: [latex] Optional: the three-point function in embedding space, in the notation of Costa, Penedones, Poland and Rychkov, Spinning Conformal Correlators (arXiv:1107.3554; cite it in the description as [@key, Eq. (...)]): points P_i, polarizations Z_i, P_{ij} = -2 P_i.P_j, V_{i,jk}, H_{ij}. A formula without $...$, shown in display math; the coefficient appears in it with any factor that the source's normalization needs (e.g. 2^{\ell/2} f). Only for a structure that is a simple embedding-space structure, or a combination the source states. See docs/THREE_POINT.md.

basis.description: Only for a structure that is one element of a basis of several independent structures of the same three-point function (n_B and n_F of <TTT>): an id shared by the elements. Values of different elements are different coefficients, each shown on its own line.

oneOf.description: [latex] The `name` of an operator in this entry's operators table, exactly as written there.

label.description: [latex] An operator that is not in the operators table (the build counts these).

operators.description: The three operators of the three-point function, as an unordered triple (the page shows them lightest first). Each value's structure assumes this order unless the value gives its own `order`.

values.description: Determinations of the coefficients of this three-point function, each the coefficient of the structure it names.

structure.description: Id of the structure whose coefficient this value is: one of data/three_point_structures.yaml or of the entry's three_point_structures.

order.description: Optional: the order of the three operators that this value's structure assumes (operator 1, 2, 3 of its form), when it is not the order of `operators`; the same three operators. A coefficient's sign can depend on it (e.g. lambda_{12O} = (-1)^l lambda_{21O} at spin l).

value_of.description: Optional: the number is the square, or the modulus, of the coefficient (e.g. lambda^2 from a bound on lambda^2, |C| when its phase is not known); omitted, it is the coefficient itself.

symbol.description: [latex] Optional: the coefficient as the source writes it, e.g. 'f_{\sigma\sigma T}', 'C_{\sigma\sigma\epsilon}'. Information only: the page writes every coefficient with one letter.

description.description: [markdown] Optional, about this value (not the convention: that is the structure's).

note.description: [markdown] Locators, assumptions, rigor, agreement with other values.
